# Regression test for 'go install' locations in GOPATH mode.
env GO111MODULE=off
[short] skip

# Binaries are installed into the GOPATH bin directory.
rm $GOPATH/bin/go-cmd-test$GOEXE
go install go-cmd-test
exists $GOPATH/bin/go-cmd-test$GOEXE

# GOBIN is removed. A value in the environment redirects nothing.
rm $GOPATH/bin/go-cmd-test$GOEXE
env GOBIN=$WORK/bin1
mkdir $WORK/bin1
go install go-cmd-test
exists $GOPATH/bin/go-cmd-test$GOEXE
! exists $WORK/bin1/go-cmd-test$GOEXE
env GOBIN=

# Installing a program outside $GOPATH fails: there is nowhere to install it.
env GOPATH= # reset to default ($HOME/go, which does not exist)
! go install go-cmd-test/helloworld.go
stderr '^go: no install location for \.go files listed on command line$'

# We can't assume that we can write to GOROOT, because it may not be writable.
# However, we can check the install location using 'go list'.
# A toolchain command installs to GOROOT/bin, never to GOPATH/bin, and a
# build tool the go command links has no target of its own.
env GOPATH=$PWD
go list -f '{{.Target}}' cmd/go/main
stdout $GOROOT'[/\\]bin[/\\]go'$GOEXE'$'
go list -f '{{.Name}} [{{.Target}}]' cmd/fix
stdout '^fix \[\]$'

-- go-cmd-test/helloworld.go --
package main

func main() {
	println("hello world")
}
